description: Corpus-attested Linear A personal names, toponyms, theonyms—partitioned by linguistic affiliation. Overlay on lexicon.json (links via lexicon_ref, never duplicates). Affiliation gated on a positive contact-DB hit or an identified reading; cognate distance alone never sets affiliation. aegean: a name read through a Linear B name or place cognate or an Egyptian Keftiu-name list, with no Semitic root (lexicon layer Aegean). All affiliations hypothetical / evidence-gated.

unknown.note: intact: at least one undamaged corpus witness; fragmentary: every witness has lost signs ([, ], [?]); edge_damaged: every sign read, but every witness sits against damaged surface (𐝫), nearly always at the word's edge, so the word may be incomplete; no_witness: no corpus group in the listed documents matches the token

One attestation.

entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: su-ki-ri-ta (Sybrita), 6 KN Da/Db livestock documents. Pre-Greek toponym; in LB it functions as a place, beside the LA attestation PH Wa 32 (cf. Davis 2026 appendix).

entries.meaning: of Sukrita (Sybrita): origin label on a jar
entries.note: Only word on side b of the HT Zb 158 jar (GORILA IV 65); side a reads [·]-TU-SE-SU-KI. Gentilic on SU-KI-RI-TA (PH Wa 32), the vowel of KI dead before RI: Sukrita, Greek Σύβριτα, a Cretan town at Thronos in the Amari valley. Ventris and Chadwick read LB su-ki-ri-ta as Sugrita, KI for /gi/; the later β is the Pre-Greek β/γ alternation of βληχών/γλαχών and βλέπω/γλέπω, not a regular labio-velar outcome (Chadwick & Baumbach 1963). Davis (Aura Suppl. 13, 46) pairs the two forms as alternating endings. -TE-I-JA has no other Linear A witness; SE-TO-I-JA (PR Za 1) shares -I-JA. The ending can be the Semitic nisba *-iy- (fem. *-iyya), the suffix of gentilics such as Ugaritic ugrty /ʾugaritiyyu/ 'man of Ugarit' (Arabic nisba, Fischer §116); Anatolian -iya- fits it as well.

entries.note: widd 'love' + ti(h)āmu 'the Deep' (Ug. thm). Sign dispute: GORILA reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading takes the fourth sign as RU.

entries.meaning: Calf of the Wild Cow (personal name, compound; wild 'young one' + rēmtu 'wild cow')
entries.note: ZA 9 .6 WI-RA-RE-MI-TE *21F 1, a recipient of one ewe (GORILA III 167). Wild-rēmti: wild 'young one', Akkadian wildu, wilid bītim (CAD I/J 71), Arabic wild (Lane 2966), + rēmti 'wild cow', Akkadian rīmtu, fRīmtum (CAD R 358–359). See the lexicon entry.

entries.meaning: the chariot soldiers: provision of wheat; rival a name ZU-*301-SE-DE
entries.note: Three words: ZU-*301 ṯannān 'chariot soldiers' (Ug. ṯnnm, DULAT 909; Hoch 1994, 261), SE-DE ṣēd 'provision', *21F-*118 ḥiṭṭa 'wheat'. A troop, not a name. Rival: a name ZU-*301-SE-DE.

entries.meaning: flute; here the flute-player, the trade of TU-QE-NU Tuqnu; rival Hurrian Tulbiya
entries.note: HT 25a .3–4 TU-QE-NU / ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, the trade after the name (GORILA I 44–45). ṯulpu 'flute', the flute-player: Ugaritic ṯlb (DULAT 892); Akk. ša šulpi 'a reed-instrument player', after a name in PN ša šu-ul-pi (CAD Š/3 257). Rival: the Hurrian name tlby (DULAT 856). One witness.

entries.note: Complete at PE Zc 4 and SY Za 2; MA 4b reads A-[?]-[?]-[?]-JA and is no witness. /ḥayyā/ '(the) Living One', √ḥ-y-y, A writing ḥ as Mari a-ia- beside ha-ia- (Weeden 2009, 96–100) (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rivals: the god Haya; the goddess Aya; Davis's 'much'.

entries.meaning: Eshmun (healing deity)
queen/princess; by metonymy the queen's or royal establishment (recipient/institutional heading)
entries.note: Corpus distribution favors a recipient, title, or institution over a 'surplus' gloss. HT105 supplies the strongest control: KA-PA and SA-RA₂ stand in parallel before VIR totals 234 and 235. The royal reading remains CANDIDATE because RA₂ is uncertain and exact Akkadian šarratu would require an unwritten final /t/.

entries.meaning: Baal, 'Lord' (allocation heading)
entries.note: PU-RA₂ occurs as an allocation heading on HT28b and HT116a. The Baal/Bōl comparison is semantically suitable but requires PU=/bV/, RA₂=/l/, loss of ʿayin, and an acknowledged U/O correspondence. The reading remains CANDIDATE and does not by itself establish a cultic document.

entries.meaning: O Diqqitu! (vocative invocation of the proposed goat-goddess Diqqitu)
entries.note: IO Za 2, position 2 of the libation formula: vocative ya- before Diqqitu, the goddess of Dikte. Ugaritic dqt 'female of small cattle for sacrifice' is a divine name in a Ugaritic god-list (Astour 1966); Hesiod calls the mountain Aigaion oros, 'Goat's Mountain'. Palaikastro writes A-DI-KI-TE and JA-DI-KI-TE-TE (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

entries.meaning: Kubaba, Sumerian Kug-Baba 'Pure is Baba' (divine or personal name)
entries.note: Conditional on PA₃=/ba/, the spelling matches Kubaba. Since Kubaba occurs as a goddess and in personal names, HT88's one-unit roster does not alone decide whether this is the deity, a woman, or a cult institution. The name and the PA₃ value must not circularly confirm one another.

entries.meaning: smith or cultic administrator; occupational title
entries.note: Recurring Haghia Triada personnel or recipient label. Arabic qayn 'smith, artisan' and Sabaic qyn 'administrator, governor' support a title; the connection with Hebrew qēnî 'Kenite' is uncertain (Biella 1982, 454).

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vow' (√n-d-r); rival Egyptian PN 'of-the-hand-of-Re'
entries.note: HT 117a personnel list (1), beside MI-TU, KU-PA₃-NU and TE-JA-RE. √n-d-r 'to vow': a name on the noun 'vow', cf. Amorite NDR (Gelb). Rival: Gordon's Egyptian personal name 'of the hand of Re'.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Linear B comparandum: no-da-ro (two vowel shifts, consonant frame n-d-r intact), KN As(1) 609 (personnel) + Dc 1228 (shepherd). A √n-d-r 'vow' name-type on both sides of the script divide, matching the Amorite NDR / Ugaritic ndr parallels.

entries.note: Daughters (fem. pl.) / Kubaba devotees (cf. KU-PA₃-NA-TU).

entries.note: Eight sealings, two hands, one deposit (Portico 11 and Room 13): one context. Rival: Amorite ila, *ilāh 'god' (Huffmon 1965, 165).

entries.meaning: Samarō, personal name, 'guard'
entries.note: HT88 KI-RO roster. √š-m-r 'guard', the Amorite name element samar (Huffmon 1965, 251). Rival: Egyptian smr 'courtier'.

entries.meaning: the enduring one (personal name)
entries.note: Retained candidate Dawmi, 'the enduring one.' The reading depends on syllabic *49=/mi/ and U≈/w/. Official *49 semantics remain PALM/TREE, with TAMIR its candidate Semitic lexical name; DA-U-PALM/TREE remains an unresolved alternative.

entries.note: A-DU (Addu) + kummi 'cella', as in SI-DU-QI-KU-MI, + the gentilic -ān of KI-RE-TA-NA: 'the one of Addu's cella'; cf. Akk. zamār kummi ana Adad 'a cella-song for Adad' (CT 15 3 i 3; CAD K 534). Beside A-KU-MI-NA on ZA 10a.

entries.meaning: Shield, Protector (invoked in formula position two); the name Tursha
entries.note: KO Za 1, invoked in formula position two, before DU-*314-RE · I-DA-A. √t-r-s 'to shield' (Ar. turs; Lane 302).

entries.meaning: Taanach (place name); rival a personal name
entries.note: Roundel label at Haghia Triada (HT Wc 3004, 3005). Amarna URU Taḫnaka, EA 248:14 (Moran 1992); Hebrew תַּעְנַךְ Taʿnak, t-ʿ-n-k with ʿ unwritten; NI against the a of Taʿnak. Place-name function on roundels unproved.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'My judgment' (short form of a √d-y-n name); rival the whole group WA-DI-NI, Ugaritic PN wḏny
entries.note: Dīnī 'My judgment', as Alalakh Dīnī-Haddu (Gelb no. 1513); after the cloth sign WA on two roundels (GORILA II 74 prints WA · DI-NI).

entries.meaning: He gave (PN, qatal 3ms of √y-t-n 'to give')—straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' same root as Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yantin-Dagan, Yattin-Dagan (Gelb 1980, nos. 2986, 3555)
entries.note: Qatal 3ms of √y-t-n. JE = /ya/ here (not /ye/), same ambiguity as LB je. Straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' paralleling Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yantin-Dagan, Yattin-Dagan (Gelb 1980, nos. 2986, 3555). Masculine counterpart of A-TA-NA-TE (ʾAtanat), the divine name that becomes Athena—feminine of the same root with I-y > ʾ weakening. Both forms attest √y-t-n productivity in Minoan onomastics. On the Haghia Triada nodule HTWa1020.

entries.meaning: personal name; Ugaritic rwy
entries.note: KN Wc 26, a roundel, RU-JA on face a and NI-PI nīb 'fruit' on face b (GORILA II 85): Ruya, the Ugaritic PN rwy (DULAT 738), the name that opens RU-JA-TA-DI Ruya-dādī. See the lexicon entry RU-JA-TA-DI.

entries.meaning: Most Righteous (PN)
entries.note: √ṣ-d-q "to be just, righteous". SA=ṣ and KA=q via emphatic neutralization in Linear A syllabary. Direct Amorite PN parallel: şadaqa (the same consonants). Cf. Hebrew Zadok (צָדוֹק), Zedekiah, Melchizedek. Attested on the Malia roundel MAWc<5> with the grain logogram GRA+E—administrative PN context. Rival: Hurrian aštaga 'woman', diminutive of ašte (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103; Laroche 1980, 61–62), which accounts for the initial A-.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'antelope'
entries.note: A recipient in the HT 108 grain list under KI-RE-TA-NA, DU-SU-NI 4[. Dišon 'antelope', as Hebrew Dîšôn. Rival: a Hurrian name in -nni.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Lion (feminine gentilic—priestess/cult title; cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA She-of-the-Bull)
entries.note: HT 25a and ZA 8. ʾarīnīt 'She-of-the-Lion': feminine -īt on ari 'lion', as I-ZU-RI-NI-TA is 'She-of-the-Bull'. A cult title rests on -īt alone, which also forms relational adjectives and abstracts. Rival: a Hurrian name in ari- 'give'.

SI-RU ṣillu 'shade, protection' (Amorite Ṣill-Haddu, Ṣillī-Baʿli) + MA-RI-TA₂ marʾ(i)tā 'the Lady' (Sabaic mrʾt 'lady, divine or human', Biella 283; Akkadian marʾatu, Aramaic mārtā): a 'Shade of DN' name with the Goddess's title.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'enduring'; compare Linear B a-ti-ka
entries.note: First word on the roundel, before A-DU-KO 2, the numeral read by Perna and Anastasiadou over GORILA's erased MI (Anastasiadou 2026, 37–39). Ugaritic ʿtq "durable" (DULAT 189); Linear B a-ti-ka, a man at Knossos (DMic I 119). See the lexicon entry.

entries.meaning: Kati-tati (Hurrian personal name); rival katītat 'beaten (oil)'
entries.note: Kati-tati: Hurrian kat- (Nuzi Qa-ti-ri, NPN 224) + -tati (Še-en-da-ti, NPN 263), the recipient heading HT 12's issue of oils, fats, wool and figs. Rival: katītat 'beaten (oil)' (semitic_roots 3644).

entries.meaning: He of Naśiʾ (personal name heading HT 126a)
entries.note: HT 126a .1 DA-NA-SI · *318 ·, heading the tablet (GORILA I 217). ḏā 'the one of' + Naśiʾ, the Amorite god written NA-SI, as in Niqmi-la-Naśiʾ NI-IQ-MI-LA-NA-SI (Gelb no. 5051) and Yadur-Naśiʾ IA-DU-UR-NA-SI (no. 3218); the 'he of DN' type of Amorite Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra (no. 6598) and DA-MI-NU. NA-SI also closes U-MI-NA-SI, the heading of HT 117a. Rival: ḏā-Nasr, the god Nasr (Q 71:23).

entries.meaning: Kaw-tatta (Hurrian personal name), kaw- + tatt- 'love'; rival Ugaritic PN kwt
entries.note: Kaw-tatta: Hurrian kaw (NPN 224) + tatt- 'love' (NPN 263), Tatta written da-da, da-da-e at Terqa (Monti 2017, 325), heading the HT 13 wine list. Cf. Kawinni, written Qa-wi-in-ni, Qa-we-en-ni, Ka-wi-ni and Ga-wi-in (NPN 224). Rival: the Ugaritic name kwt (DULAT 469).

entries.meaning: Kawṯuni (Hurrian personal name Kaw-šuni); rival Kawṯān, Heb. Kûšān
entries.note: Kawṯuni: Hurrian kaw (NPN 224) + -šuni (Awa-šuni, NPN 208), Hurrian š written ṯ as Ugaritic ảủpṯ for ảủpš (DULAT 4), four men on HT 26b. Same base as KA-U-DE-TA Kaw-tatta. Rival: Kawṯān, Heb. Kûšān (DULAT 467).

entries.meaning: Timar the Levite (f.), priestess (woman's name and title); rival Tamar + WI-TE
entries.note: PY R 1 .1–2 TI-MA-RU-WI-TE, a ligature and VIN 90, the only entry (GORILA I 322). Tīmar 'palm', final r unwritten, + luwwīt, fem. of luwwī as in DU-RU-WI: name and title, as Minaean lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay' (M 333). Rival: TA-MA-RU Tamar (Gelb no. 6027) + WI-TE.

entries.meaning: Kiriš, the god of the Amorite names, as oil recipient; rivals Hurrian Kiriš and a personal name
entries.note: Amorite DN Kiriš (Mari: ARM XIV 106:18, ARM XIII 8:19; Nakata 1995: 7 name types; seal of Iluna-Kiriš). Not Elamite Kiririša. Rival: Hurrian kir + -š (Gelb 1944: 113). TY3b KI-RI-SI OLE+MI 6.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Sūka—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt
personal name, 'with me (is God)', hypocoristic in -aya (cf. Hebrew ʾIttay)
entries.note: Heb. ʾIttay (2 Sam 15:19); NA {m}i-ta-a-a (Schøyen 52).
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: i-ta-ja, KN Ap 769 (women personnel) + Od(1) 537 (wool). Screening caveat: could be Greek-formed ethnicon *Idaiā 'of Ida', though Ida is itself a pre-Greek oronym—either way the base is substrate.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'our Beloved'
entries.note: widd 'love' (Lane 2931); Arabian names wdn, wdnt (Harding 1971, 639). Rival: Wadd, a god.

entries.meaning: Sleepy (personal name); rival √y-š-š 'aged'
entries.note: √w-š-n 'to sleep'; the Ugarit name yšn, ia-ši-nu (DULAT 973), Hebrew Yāšēn (HALOT 448). Rival: √y-š-š 'aged'.

entries.meaning: (Little) kinsman (personal name, hypocoristic); rival ʾAmaya 'maidservant'
entries.note: KH 14 .1 ]RA · A-MA-JA · CYP 6[, whole between dividers (GORILA III 45). A-MA ʿamma 'kinsman' + -ya: the Ugaritic name ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 4.16:4), syllabic am-ma-ya (DULAT 164). Rival: ʾAmaya 'maidservant'.

entries.meaning: Good (f.) (personal name)
entries.note: A recipient on two Zakros tablets by different scribes: 1 in the ZA 10a name list, 2½ on ZA 8, both intact. ṭayyibat- 'good (f.)': Amorite DA-BA-TUM Ṭaybatum, a woman (Gelb no. 1409), DA for ṭ. Same spelling as Linear B da-i-pi-ta, opening KN B 799 beside ke-do-si-ja (Killen, Mycenaean Greek, glossary): the name survives into Mycenaean Knossos. Rival: DA-I + PI-TA.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: da-i-pi-ta, KN Bk 799+8306—Davis's canonical ZA 10 example of Minoan name continuity (Docs² 537): the ZA10a name list and a Knossos tablet carry the identical four-syllable name, non-Greek per Docs².

entries.meaning: Addar, 'Mighty' (personal name)
entries.note: Recipient beside A-DU-NI-TA-NA on ARKH5, with GRA 40[+ and *131B 6. Final -O a dead vowel.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the True One' (kīnu 'true, reliable')
Kret (eponym of Crete)
entries.note: HT 85b and HT 129, allocation context; written with TA₂, where KI-RE-TA and the gentilic KI-RE-TA-NA have TA. Kirēta, cf. Ugaritic krt /kirta/, the king of the Kirta epic (KTU 1.14–16). Rival: the island's own name, a pre-Greek toponym later fitted to √k-r-t.

entries.meaning: Kret (variant spelling)
entries.note: HT 114a and HT 121, paired with SA-RA₂ in one allocation template: Kirīta, KI-RE-TA₂ Kirēta with RI for RE, Ugaritic krt /kirta/, the king of the Kirta epic (Huehnergard 2012, 60). See the lexicon entries KI-RI-TA₂ and KI-RE-TA₂.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Linear B match: ki-ri-ta, KN Ld(2) 785 (textile series). Same crux as KI-RI-TA (q.v.): Greek krithā 'barley' competes for the LB form.

entries.meaning: ʾItniša (personal name), the Mari name IT-NU-ŠA; rival ʾitnī-ša 'her gift (portion)'
entries.note: ʾItniša, the Mari name IT-NU-ŠA (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 610, no. 3828), a recipient of wine 10 on ZA 15a. Rival: ʾitnī-ša 'her gift (portion)' (DULAT 119).

entries.meaning: my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink—theonym plus compound divine epithet
entries.note: IO Za 6, position 2 of the libation formula, complete and undivided: I-NA-TA-I ʿInatī 'my Anat' + ZU-DI ṯudī 'breast' + SI-KA šiqā 'she who gives drink'. Initial I carries ʿ, as syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ and ša-i for /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). Ugaritic gives Anat the title ṯd lʾimm 'the breast of the people' (KTU 1.13:19). See the lexicon entry.

entries.meaning: personal name (Mitanni Indo-Aryan type)
entries.note: Compare Nuzi Mittar-atti, element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI), Mitanni Indo-Aryan *mitra-atthi- 'having Mitra [or a friend] as his guest' (Gentile 2019, 157). Rival: Indo-Aryan -mitta, as Amarna Ša-mitta.

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), on √ś-y-m 'to place, fix'; rival Šimʿat
entries.note: HT 96a .2 SI-MI-TA GRA 5, the first recipient (GORILA I 156). Śīmat, the women's name of Amorite ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM (Gelb no. 5893). Rival: Hebrew Šimʿat (2 Kgs 12:22). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, as Ugaritic Kušinu (kṯn)
entries.note: HT 85a KU-ZU-NI 5, in a roster counted under VIR; HT 13 KU-ZU-NI 18, in the KA-U-DE-TA wine list (KU-RO 130½). Ugaritic kṯn, syllabic ku-ši-nu (Kinlaw 1967, 76), ki-še-na, etym. unc. (DULAT s.v. kṯn (I)); ZU writes ṯ. Rival: Ug. ktn 'tunic', which has t, not ṯ.

entries.meaning: waitress, girl (Ug. ṯdr, a Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri); rival the name Šituri
entries.note: Roundels HTWc 3011 and 3012; a third reading *79-DI-RA is HTWc 3012 again. ṯudira 'waitress, girl': Ugaritic ṯdr (DULAT 886), a Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri 'young woman' (Laroche 1980, 229; CAD Š/2 408). Rival: the Hurrian woman's name Šituri 'Girl', ši-du-ri at Mari and ši-tu-ri at Ašnakkum (Monti 2017, 296, 373). See the lexicon entry.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Hired' (article ha- + SI-KI-RA); rival haśkira 'he rewarded'
entries.note: KH 20 .1 A-SI-KI-RA · CYP+E ⅓, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA (GORILA III 51). ha-Śikira 'the Hired': the article ha- + SI-KI-RA (HT 8a), √ś-k-r 'to hire'. Rival: haśkira 'he rewarded', and the Amorite DN ʾAškur (Gelb nos. 947, 950). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, '(a bird)', Akk. būṣu; rival an institution; a recipient
entries.note: Recipient or institution: HT123+124b PI-SA 4; KH6 .6 PI-SA[ at a line end, broken after (GORILA III 27), where SigLA reads CYP+D ½ next. Amorite Bu-ṣí, with PI for b and SA for ṣ. Rival: an institution receiving allocations.

entries.note: Beside PU-RA₂ (Bōlu) on HT28b.

entries.note: Qualifier after a personal name: HT115a RI-TA-MA / NU-WI 2; HT115b TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½. See lexicon NU-WI.

entries.meaning: Piṭrī, personal name, 'my release'
entries.note: Candidate name in PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE, proposed 'Pitrī, the priest'; compare Ugaritic pṭry and Amorite Annu-puṭri and Ištar-puṭri. Rival: Gordon's pi-te za 'this engraved monument' (1966, §124). See lexicon PI-TE-RI.

entries.meaning: the priest (proposed title after PI-TE-RI)
entries.note: Candidate singular priestly title in apposition to PI-TE-RI. Root √k-h-n is secure; the article, vocalization, and treatment of /h/ remain reconstructed. See lexicon A-KO-A-NE.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Hired' (√ś-k-r 'to hire'); rival šēkār 'strong drink'
entries.note: HT 8a, a recipient of KI-oil ¼ between QA-*310-I and KI-RE-TA-NA, in the list with TE-*301 Tēnā 'Fig'. Mari Sa-ki-rum and the woman's name Sa-ki-ra, under *škr 'hire, reward, favor' (Huffmon, APNM 245–46). Rival: šēkār 'strong drink'. A-SI-KI-RA (KH 20) is the same name with the article ha-. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vineyard' (√k-r-m)
entries.note: HT 117a, one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10): a name on the noun 'vineyard', as TE-*301 Tēnā 'Fig'. Hebrew kerem, Ugaritic krm. One witness.

entries.meaning: Fattened (personal name), the bare stem of the Amorite MARUʾ- names; rival Maru 'Wool'
entries.note: HT 117a, one of ten men counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10), between KU-RA-MU and KU-PA₃-NU. Amorite names open with MA-RU on MRʾ (Gelb 1980, nos. 4542, 4543, 4545); *mrʾ 'fat cattle', Ugaritic mrủ 'fatling' (DULAT 563). Rival: Maru 'Wool', the wool word of logogram MA+RU. See the lexicon entry.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Merciful (god)'; rival tayyār 'trader'
entries.note: HT 117a, one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10), before NA-DA-RE: Ugarit has the man's name Tiyaru, ti-ya-ru₃ (RS 14.0016 r 3); Akkadian tajjāru 'merciful (god)' in Sîn-tayyār, Tayyār-ilu (AHw 1304). Rival: tayyār 'trader' (√t-w-r). See the lexicon entry. One witness.

entries.meaning: the Kushite woman (origin label); rival kusītu 'robe'
entries.note: HT 117a, the second of five counted 1 each under SA-TA, between KU-KU-DA-RA and DA-MI-NU: the feminine nisbe of Kōš 'Kush' (Coptic ⲉϭⲱϣ; Amarna ka-ši-yi, EA 287:33), an origin label as U-SU and U-DI-MI. Rival: kusītu 'robe'. See the lexicon entry. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'palm'
entries.note: KO(?) Zf 2, a bronze bowl, inside the undivided sequence A-RA-KO-KU-QA-WA-SA-TO-MA-RO-AU-TA-DE-PO-NI-ZA: a palm name, Amorite Tamar-u (Gelb 1980, no. 6027), Ugaritic tmr, Hebrew Tāmār. See the lexicon entry. One witness.

entries.meaning: water(-men), water-drawers of the sanctuary; rival Anatolian 'grown-ups'

entries.meaning: the (district) of Qīr, the walled town; heading opposite KA-PA 'village'; rival diḳaru 'pot'
entries.note: KA-PA and DA-QE-RA head the two sections of HT 6a; DA-QE-RA heads HT 120, grain to DA-ME, KI-RE-TA-NA and PA-I-TO, and HT 57a. ḏā 'the one of' + Qīr, a town name, Moabite qr 'city', Hebrew Qîr Môʾāb (HALOT 1099–1100). Rival: diqāru 'bowl' (CAD D 157). See the lexicon entry.
